subject: FY28 planning signal: target bands, contingency ladders & QBR prep
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FY28 planning signal: target bands, contingency ladders & QBR prep

Team — kicking off a short, targeted planning thread to align on (A) target bands for FY28, (B) contingency ladders if growth falls short, and (C) the QBR-ready artifacts we need by early Aug. Goal: firm up targets and an execution-ready contingency playbook so sales + finance can finalize guidance by 8/10.

High-level asks for this week: 
- Markus: run two velocity scenarios (Base / Down-10%) and propose top-3 levers for recapture. See attached FY28_target_bands_v1.xlsx.
- Marissa: propose a condensed QBR narrative and owner list for FY28 (sales, CS, product).
- Lauren: confirm regional headcount impacts for the target bands and surface any hiring freeze risk.
- Jonas: alignment on the canary/fallback model routing policy we discussed — impacts OPS cost curve.
- Stephanie: compile the list of cross-functional approvals & procurement windows we need for Dedicated contracts and renewals.

Timeline I propose:
- By Thu 6/17: initial scenario numbers + QBR skeleton
- Week of 6/21: iteration with finance and product leads
- 7/5: consolidated recommendation to execs

Attachments: FY28_target_bands_v1.xlsx (tabbed targets + assumptions), scenario_ladders_v1.pdf (visual), QBR_prep_timeline.docx (draft dates).

Notes on scope: keep this to high-confidence levers — pricing/packaging moves are a separate thread. If external deal timing (Acme, BetaHealth) materially changes numbers, call it out in the scenario sheet.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FY28 planning signal: target bands, contingency ladders & QBR prep

Thanks Priya — looked through the spreadsheet. Quick notes: 
1) Base assumptions: converted trial-to-paid and funnel velocity look sensible but I want to surface one sensitivity: renewals that cross into dedicated committed capacity can create step changes in both unit economics and gross. I added a small tab called "Committed-cliffs" in FY28_target_bands_v1.xlsx.
2) For the Down-10% ladder, I ran a scenario that sequences (A) tighter batching/caching thresholds, (B) 90-day delay on non-essential hiring, (C) temporary cap on burst capacity — see attached scenario_ladders_me_v1.pdf. Estimated P&L impact and headcount delta on tab 3.
3) Suggest adding a short table in the QBR artifact that clarifies which customers trigger tiered pricing/committed discounts (useful when we talk Acme).

Attachment: scenario_ladders_me_v1.pdf (detailed lever sequencing).

I'll sync with Finance on Thursday to validate the P&L deltas. Markus
Markus Klein
GM, Americas | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FY28 planning signal: target bands, contingency ladders & QBR prep

Agree with Markus' approach. Couple of practical pieces for the QBR artifact: 
- Recommend a 1-page executive summary (target band, primary risk, top 3 mitigations) + 3 supporting slides (metrics, levers, timeline). I'll draft the 1-pager and assign owners.
- Proposed owners: Sales narrative (Marissa), CS impact appendix (Lauren), Product deployment risks (Jonas), Ops cost impact (Markus), Finance reconciliation (Stephanie).
- We should lock the QBR skeleton by Friday 6/18 so we have time to get finance input the week of 6/21.

I'll attach a starter deck outline. Also — Acme has asked for visibility into our FY28 targets for their renewal planning; Markus/Stephanie please flag any guidance we should pre-clear with legal/procurement before sharing.

Attachment: QBR_skeleton_v1.pptx

— Marissa
VP, GTM Strategy | Redwood Inference

Two operational flags: 
1) The canary/fallback routing policy we discussed reduces short-term latency but increases tail-storage costs in the model. If we lean into it as a lever, Ops needs a clear rollback trigger (I suggest "tail-cost > 4% of gross for 14 consecutive days").
2) We have an engineering offsite the week of 6/21 that will limit my availability for synchronous reviews. If we still want a mid-week check-in, recommend shifting the timeline one day earlier (lock by Thu 6/17 instead of Fri 6/18) so we have a clean week for finance to validate numbers.

Otherwise, I support the structure. Jonas
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
